title: 'It F***ing Sucks, and in a Way Is a Compliment' — Resident Evil Requiem Is Proving Tough for Fans With Arachnophobia, Though the Inevitable Thomas the Tank Engine Mod Is Here to Help
body_text: Related reads:Capcom Hid an Enormous Secret About Leon S. Kennedy That You'll Only Realize After Resident Evil Requiem's Credits Roll Arachnophobia sufferers are having a tough time with Resident Evil Requiem, but there is help at hand from fellow players — as well as in the shape of a certain cheery choo choo train. Warning: Spoilers for Resident Evil Requiem followRequiem features a giant spider as a major boss fight in Raccoon City, and the knowledge that this sequence is in the game has spawned many, many, many different threads on reddit from Resident Evil fans who experience arachnophobia. In most cases, fans are requesting more information on how horrible the game's spider section is (it's quite horrible), while others who made it through the battle are reporting in with their experiences. Some fans are stuck in a dilemma — they want to play the big new Resident Evil game, but are also dreading reaching a section with a very realistic giant spider boss that's creepy enough even for those without an actual phobia."Trying to be as vague as possible in the title, how is that f***ing giant spider mid-game?" reads one such message, from reddit user saekhama. "Does it come in a jumpscare or you can predict the moment it's gonna make its first appearance/attack? For reference, I'd say the Skyrim and Witcher 3 spiders are some of the worst, as they're hairy, realistic and move fast. I don't think I'm gonna not buy the game because of it, but I might ask a friend to come and play this part for me.""It's horrible," answered another fan, Tasty_James, in reply. "As someone who can't get through the Aragog/Shelob scenes in their respective [Harry Potter and Lord of the Rings] films, this has been a f***ing nightmare. It's huge, hairy, detailed, and f***ing fast... Genuinely the most terrifying experience I’ve ever had during any videogame (and I could probably expand that to all media as well, tbh).In other discussion threads, players have been offering tips on how to kill the spider boss fast, in order to get it off their screens as quickly as possible."I got to the spider boss section! I wasn't expecting that until the last minute I was like 'Wait a damn minute... these are webs!' took me a while to realize it then BOOM, big spooder: Hello There >:)" wrote TheSkateDude6. "How many shots or melee attacks does it take to finish it off? I'll be playing without my glasses since it will help slightly in a way. If it's too much for me, I'll wait for an arachnophobia mode." Common tips for this section are to make use of the areas explosive barrels, and of course your Requiem gun. (IGN's walkthrough also has plenty of advice — and you can find the spider boss fight section here.) Some fans with arachnophobia have reported using less conventional tactics, meanwhile, such as playing without wearing their glasses, or even moving to a smaller TV screen."My strategy so far has been to take off my glasses (I'm severely near-sighted)," Tasty_James said, "and sort of look vaguely away from the screen so as to keep it blurry and in my peripheral vision at all times. I haven't beaten its boss fight yet, obviously, and I have no idea if I'm going to be able to.""I played this without my glasses, it's a blessing in disguise somehow," wrote Typical-Mixture4376 in another thread. "The smaller ones are freaking me out more than the large one lol," EqualAd-1348 wrote, in yet another conversation. "Thankfully, I think I will at least be able to manage by playing that segment on my other TV (32")."As well as an enormous spider that Leon has to fight, a swarm of mini baby spiders is also featured as part of the same area. On the upside, though, once outside of the one spider section, the game does not feature the enemies ever again. "It was genuinely the worst experience I've ever had with my arachnophobia in a video game," concluded TheUberMensch123. "It fucking sucks, and in a way is a complement, that the thing moves and looks so goddamn real. I almost had to shut the game off. Hopefully an arachnophobia mod comes out soon."While there isn't an arachnophobia mode add-on yet, NexusMods does host the customary Thomas the Tank Engine mod. While unavailable on consoles, PC players can at least choo choo choose to see Thomas' giant smiling face bearing down upon Leon rather than that of an enormous arachnid. We'll leave it up to you to decide which is worse.Choo choo! https://t.co/Ax5AFzhVEk pic.twitter.com/dsZFt2SIBN— ?️‍? ΛLISTΞR ?️‍? (@xZombieAlix) March 2, 2026 Whether you're battling spiders or zombies, IGN's Resident Evil: Requiem guide will help you every step of the way through RE9. Take note of these key tips and tricks before you get started, and focus on finding these important items early. Plus, our comprehensive walkthrough will make sure you don't miss a single Bobblehead or file as you try to survive from the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center all the way to Raccoon City.Image credit: xZombieAlix.Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social Related reads:Resident Evil Requiem Criticized for 'Immersion-Breaking' Gore Censorship in Japan

title: Nintendo Indie World Showcase March 2026: Everything Announced
body_text: Related reads:AliExpress Has a Pair of Nintendo Switch Joy-Con 2 Controllers for Just $83 (Normally $100) Nintendo just presented its latest Indie World Showcase, and it was filled with indie games headed to Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. From Blue Prince being out today to new looks and release dates for Mixtape, Denshattack!, Rotwood, Blighted, and much more, there was a lot to be excited about.We've gathered all the announcements from the Nintendo Indie World Showcase right here to ensure you didn't miss a thing, and we'd love to know with reveal was your favorite!Blue Prince Will Bring Its Mind-Bending Puzzles to Switch TodayFor the 'one last thing' of today's Nintendo Indie World Showcase, it was revealed that the mind-bending puzzler known as Blue Prince will be released on Nintendo Switch 2 later today. Step into Mt. Holly, a peculiar manor that features ever-changing rooms, and it's up to you to find its enigmatic Room 46. Mixtape Is Officially Headed to Nintendo Switch 2Mixtape is officially heading to Nintendo Switch 2 on May 7, 2026, and will let you follow three friends on their last night of high school who go on a grand adventure together by playing through a mixtape of memories, set to a "soundtrack of a generation" that features DEVO, The Smashing Pumpkins, and more.Mixtape will also be available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.Denshattack! Kicks Off the Nintendo Indie World Showcase In StyleDenshattack!, the game lovingly referred to as Tony Hawk with Japanese trains, kicked off the Nintendo Indie World showcase by revealing new gameplay, sharing its June 17 release date for Nintendo Switch 2 and announcing that a demo is available today! Oh, and players can also get an exclusive train skin if they purchase at launch.Rotwood Is a Nintendo Switch 2 Console Exclusive From Don't Starve's Klei EntertainmentDon't Starve developer Klei Entertainment has revealed Rotwood, a stylish side-scrolling co-op action brawler that will let you play solo or with up to three friends. Klei also notes that increasing your skill is just as important as the loot you gather, so make sure you are ready as Rotwood is out today! Drinkbox Studios' Blighted Needs You to Reclaim Your People's Memory Before You Are DevouredDrinkbox Studios has revealed Blighted, an upcoming game where you will need to "journey through a corrupt world to reclaim the memories of your people before the Blight devours you." You are the lone survivor of an attack by the evil Sorcisto, and but you will be able to bring along a friend if you so choose.Blighted will be released on Switch 2 this fall.Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault Needs You to Be the Best Shopkeeper and Dungeon ExplorerDungeon-crawler by day, merchant by night. Clear hostile biomes and sell the loot you discover in Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault from @DigitalSunGames. Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2026! #IndieWorld pic.twitter.com/e6HkKRyHSc— Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) March 3, 2026 Run a shop and go explore dungeons in Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault. The further you delve, the greater the reward, but it won't be easy. You'll have to master both parts of your life when Moonlight 2: The Endless Vault launches later in 2026. My Little Puppy Looks to Be a Heartwarming Tale of Our Best Friends After They Cross the Rainbow BridgeAfter escaping doggy heaven, help Bong-gu the Welsh Corgi run, bark, and sniff his way through the afterlife in search of his dad. My Little Puppy from @MLP_Dreamotion jumps onto Nintendo Switch digitally on May 29, with a physical release in June! #IndieWorld pic.twitter.com/oNzwZ2D0Z9— Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) March 3, 2026 My Little Puppy is headed to Switch on May 29, 2026, and it looks to tell a heartwarming tale of our best friends after they cross the rainbow bridge. This game stars a Welsh Corgi named Bong-gu who smells the scent of his human dad in the afterlife, and this sets players on an adventure all about "relationships, farewells, and reuinions." The Switch version of My Little Puppy also features costume customization for Bong-gu, which will surely also melt our hearts in the best way!Heave Ho 2 Is a Party Game Where You Need to 'Grab What You Can and Swing to Win!'Heave Ho 2 is a ridiculously wonderful-looking party game that tasks your and up to three friends to "grab what you can and swing to win!" It looks like a chaotically great time and will be available on Switch, Switch 2, and PC in summer 2026.Deadzone: Rogue Is an FPS Sci-Fi Roguelike That Wants You to Come Back Stronger Every TimeStep into a forsaken space station in @DeadzoneRogue, an FPS roguelite where every run is a heated fight for survival. Blast through hostile machines solo or with friends on Nintendo Switch 2 on March 17! #IndieWorld pic.twitter.com/26k2WwSmyy— Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) March 3, 2026 Come aboard a forsaken space station infested with biomechanical threats that will challenge you at every turn in Deadzone: Rogue. This upcoming FPS Sci-Fi Roguelike encourages you to keep coming back stronger than before, and to do so by scavenging and combining experimental weaponry to become the ultimate killing machine. Deadzone: Rogue will be released on Nintendo Switch 2 on March 17, 2026.Minishoot' Adventures Arrives on Nintendo Switch 1 & 2 TodayMinishoot' Adventures is a game with a unique mix of action-adventure exploration and twin-stick shooting, and it's out on Nintendo Switch 1 & 2 later today! You play as a ship you'll need to upgrade, and your journey will take you to caverns, ancient temples, sunken cities, and more. Woodo Is a Cozy 3D Diorama Game That Already has Our HeartsRevive wooden scenes piece by piece and let them bloom with color and life! Woodo from @daedalic is a cozy diorama puzzle game, coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch this summer. #IndieWorld pic.twitter.com/r6AZYOgH7r— Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) March 3, 2026 Follow the story of Foxy the Fox and the Ben the Frog while you get cozy and build 3D dioramas that have already stolen our hearts. The devs describe it as a 3D coloring book, and the scene fills in every time you place a piece in its correct spot. Woodo will be available in summer 2026.The Midnight Walk Is a Dark Fantasy Adventure Built in Real-Life Clay and Animated in a Stop Motion StyleLost in Random and Fe's The Midnight Walk is a dark fantasy adventure that was built in real-life clay and animated in a stop motion style that is both gorgeous and terrifying. You will become the Burnt One, befriend a lost lantern creature named Potboy, and use his flame to help you find your way.The Midnight Walk Launches on March 26.Nintendo Indie World Showcase Teases Even More Games Headed to Nintendo Switch 1 & 2The Nintendo Indie World Showcase presented us with an exciting montage filled with even more games headed to both Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2, and they included Outbound (April 23, demo out today!), Unrailed 2: Back on Track (May, demo out today!), TOEM 2 (Summer), Ratatan (July 16), inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories (April 30), and Grave Seasons (Summer). Developing...Adam Bankhurst is a news writer for IGN. You can follow him on Twitter @AdamBankhurst and on Twitch. title: Pokémon Pokopia Becomes the Highest-Rated Pokémon Game of All-Time
body_text: Related reads:Pokémon Pokopia Review Pokémon Pokopia has become the highest-rated Pokémon game of all time on Metacritic. The building and town simulator is sitting on a Metascore of 88 on Metacritic. That not only makes it one of the highest-reviewed games of the year so far — it's currently sitting alongside Mewgenics, RPG Estoreic Ebb, and Resident Evil Requiem — but that also makes it the highest-rated Pokémon game ever.While Pokémon Y also has an 88 Metascore, Pokémon X has an 87, slightly lowering the average across both 2013 3DS games. That means Pokopia also pips Pokémon Moon, Pokémon HeartGold, Pokémon Black, Pokémon White, Pokémon SoulSilver, and Pokémon Sun, all of which boast a very respectable Metacritic score of 87.Pokémon Pokopia sees you play as a Ditto that has transformed to look like a human and must shape an empty land into a beautiful space for a variety of Pokémon. You'll learn new moves from Pokémon you meet to expand and create a paradise, collecting berries, rocks, and wood, as well as building furniture, growing vegetables in fields you’ve tilled, creating homes for Pokémon you meet, and more.IGN's Pokémon Pokopia review returned a 9. We said: "Pokémon Pokopia is an enjoyable, personality-packed building simulator set in a surprisingly deep world that is stuffed with fun things for its delightful Ditto protagonist to do and create." It's out on March 5 exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.Wondering which Pokémon you'll be able to live alongside? Check out our list of all the Pokémon in Pokopia, and stay tuned to the IGN Pokopia Wiki for more guides when Pokopia arrives on March 5.Vikki Blake is a reporter for IGN, as well as a critic, columnist, and consultant with 15+ years experience working with some of the world's biggest gaming sites and publications. She's also a Guardian, Spartan, Silent Hillian, Legend, and perpetually High Chaos. Find her at BlueSky. Related reads:All Confirmed Pokemon in Pokemon Pokopia

title: Battlefield 6's New Patch Addresses QoL and Stability Issues, As Well As UI and Battle Pass
body_text: Related reads:Battlefield 6 Season 2 Gets Roadmap and First Gameplay Trailer Following Delay Battlefield 6 has unveiled what's changing with update 1.2.1.5, which rolls out today (March 3).Focusing on quality-of-life improvements and stability fixes, the new patch expects to resolve "several issues across gameplay," including its UI, Battle Pass, and Battle Royale. This update also restores missing store content and addresses "critical revive and gadget interactions." Here's what's rolling on to consoles and PCs later today.Major Updates for 1.2.1.5Implemented additional stability improvements to reduce client crashes.Improved frontend tile loading times for a smoother menu experience.Restored missing Store items to player inventory from the Bountiful Harvest, Pax Vanguard, and Devil Dogs bundles.CHANGELOGPLAYERAddressed a crash that could occur during camera behaviour transitions.Implemented further stability improvements to reduce client crashes.Resolved an issue where initiating a revive while equipping a mask could cause the mask to remain in hand and block weapon usage.Restored previously owned items that had disappeared from player inventories, including content from the Bountiful Harvest, Pax Vanguard, and Devil Dogs bundles.WEAPONSImproved the visual fidelity of the Objective Ace skin when viewed at longer distances.MAPS & MODESUpdated spawn logic with an additional out-of-combat area check to prevent unintended spawn locations.UI & HUDCorrected an issue where the Tier Skip deeplink in the Bulletin directed players to an empty Store screen.Improved frontend tile loading times to reduce delays when navigating menus.Resolved an issue where Battle Pass rewards on the active path could display placeholder text or missing icons.PORTALAddressed a crash related to area validation checks.REDSECPLAYERResolved an issue in Battle Royale where the Tracking Pulse Recon trait could activate when destroying any deployable gadget.UI & HUDAddressed an issue in Battle Royale Duos where pings were not displayed in the elimination feed.AUDIOResolved an issue in Gauntlet where Gas Mask voice-over lines would play while inside armoured vehicles.Battlefield 6 got off to a strong start in 2025 but has faced backlash from its community in recent months, bringing its Steam user score down to 'Mixed.' As some players review-bombed its battle royale REDSEC offshoot and others pleaded for larger maps, many began to question if two maps per season were enough to keep players engaged. Confusion then reached new levels in January, when EA and BF Studios announced Season 2 was delayed to February 17.While we wait to see how the team plans to continue building on Battlefield 6, you can read about some of the ways BF Studios is adjusting its controversial cosmetics.Vikki Blake is a reporter for IGN, as well as a critic, columnist, and consultant with 15+ years experience working with some of the world's biggest gaming sites and publications. She's also a Guardian, Spartan, Silent Hillian, Legend, and perpetually High Chaos. Find her at BlueSky. title: 'Don't Think for a Second That We're Gonna Remove the SAUCE From the UI' — Marathon Dev Doubles Down on 'Fontslop'
body_text: Related reads:Marathon Confirms Seasonal Resets, Which Means Everyone's Gear, Contract and Faction Progression, and Player Level Wipe Every Few Months Marathon’s user interface has become one of the game’s chief talking points, with some calling it confusing, unintuitive, and cluttered. One of the criticisms has to do with the sheer number of different fonts on-screen at any one time. Bungie’s Marathon is certainly striking, visually, but some think it has too much going on for its own good, accusing it of being “fontslop.”Marathon gotta be the first ever fontslop gameThere's like 20 different combinations of fonts, boldness levels, sizes, spacing, all caps vs regular caps, all on one menu pageJust an absolute eye sore ?They REALLY need to pull back on the whole "abstract" thing for the UI pic.twitter.com/Ra89yB8dhp— Kelski (@kelskiYT) February 27, 2026 While Bungie has indicated it’s receptive to feedback on Marathon’s UI and will tweak it post-launch, Elliott Gray, who works on user interface design on Marathon, took to social media to double down on the ‘fontslop’ claims, jokingly describing himself as the “fontslop merchant” and using the hashtag #fontsloptakeover.Gray also said that while Bungie will respond to player feedback, “don't think for a second that we're gonna remove the SAUCE from the UI.”all jokes aside there's plenty of work we can and will do as a team to respond to player feedback about inventory management, navigation, density of info, etc... ...but don't think for a second that we're gonna remove the SAUCE from the UI. #fontsloptakeover https://t.co/HOUlzT9Uwv— elliott (@elliottgray) March 2, 2026 To me, that suggests Bungie will stick to its guns on Marathon’s UI, at least when it comes to its fundamental visual design. Sure, we can expect some improvements (I hope Bungie makes items a lot clearer in your inventory!), but those fonts sound immovable.There’s a lot of talk, generally, about Marathon’s design and whether or not Bungie will tweak it as the game hurtles towards its March 5 release date. For example, Bungie has acknowledged the debate around TTK (time to kill), which is ultra fast in Marathon. During the Server Slam, players found that they could be killed extremely quickly, with their shields and health bar gone in the blink of an eye. Enemy players are of course extremely dangerous in the extraction shooter, but the AI enemies are just as brutal. Turn around the wrong corner and you can find yourself eliminated before you can react, the run over and all your gear lost forever.“We've learned a lot from you, watched from the shadows as you've hit snags or found moments of glory, and taken notes the whole time,” Bungie said in its Server Slam weekend feedback recap. “Your input during this time has given us a lot of items to sort through and we'll be doing just that in the coming days, so thank you.”Another point of feedback Bungie acknowledged was on the med and ammo economy. Players have found both sets of items scarce, to the point where it’s easy to run out of ammo, especially, making Marathon an even tougher experience than it already is. When you factor in the in-game cost associated with replenishing med and ammo items for each run, you can see why both are precious commodities.“We hear you that meds are soaking a lot of your early loadout budget and that back-to-back fights can chew through your med and ammo reserves pretty quickly,” Bungie said. “We've seen some folks for and against the Depleted items as well — along with how rewarding drops off of AI are. If you ran dry mid-fight or at a critical spot in your Run, tell us all about it!”The Marathon Server Slam hit a peak Steam concurrent player count of 143,621 when it launched last week, but somewhat surprisingly, that number declined as we worked through the weekend. Marathon hit a peak of 64,128 concurrents on Sunday, just a few days before Marathon goes on sale priced $39.99 on March 5. Of course, Steam concurrents do not paint the entire picture, and neither Sony nor Microsoft makes player numbers public. It will be interesting to see how Marathon does at launch.Speaking of which, Bungie said the Server Slam “was only a slice of Marathon’s gameplay and progression.”Launch will bring the full faction and contract progression, all six launch Runner shells (including Thief), and three zones (including Outpost), Bungie confirmed. The end-game zone, Cryo Archive, on the UESC Marathon ship and Ranked mode are also coming during Season 1, along with “other surprises.”Check out IGN's Marathon review so far to find out what we think.Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me. Related reads:Marathon Review So Far

title: Capcom Pulls Enigma DRM From Resident Evil 4 Remake, Following Performance Complaints
body_text: Related reads:How to Play the Resident Evil Games in Chronological Order Capcom has removed a controversial new form of DRM from Resident Evil 4 Remake, following complaints that its recent addition was impacting performance. An update to the game's Steam database listing shows that the Enigma DRM was removed earlier today, March 3, after an earlier listing showing its addition at the beginning of February. Capcom has not commented publicly on the changes, though fans were quick to spot the publisher replacing the game's previous Denuvo anti-piracy protection with Enigma, and the hit to performance that followed. It's a subject recently covered by Digital Foundry, whose tests showed a 40 percent deficit in performance within the game's intro cutscenes, though more modest differences during gameplay. In a video published last month, DF's Alex Battaglia noted that Denuvo was believed to operate as a subscription service, and that at some point publishers typically remove the software when its cost outweighs any perceived losses from piracy. It's at this point that fans believe Capcom switched to Enigma instead — a decision it has now seemingly U-turned on. "Updating years old software with new DRM is just stupid," Battaglia said. "Like, stop, don't do that in the first place. Regardless of any possible performance degradations, what it'll do to your game is just piss off your audience. It'll make your modding scene really upset."Now, word that Enigma DRM is gone from Resident Evil 4 is being celebrated by fans on reddit, even as the decision to add it in the first place is being criticized. "This was the most mid level executive that's detached from gaming move I've seen," wrote Resident Evil fan CoDog. "Like who would've thought it was a good idea to put in DRM on a two year old game that's been regularly on sale that tanks low to mid level pc hardware's performance? Seriously mind boggling move from Capcom."It sounds like a good time to revisit Resident Evil 4 Remake, though not before you're done with the brilliant Resident Evil Requiem first. If you're still exploring Leon S. Kennedy's latest adventure then IGN's Resident Evil: Requiem guide will help you every step of the way through RE9. Take note of these key tips and tricks before you get started, and focus on finding these important items early. Plus, our comprehensive walkthrough will make sure you don't miss a single Bobblehead or file as you try to survive from the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center all the way to Raccoon City.Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social Related reads:20 Years On Capcom Can't Escape the Shadow of Resident Evil 4

title: Update: Iron Galaxy Denies Speculation It's Working on a Fallout: New Vegas Remaster
body_text: Related reads:Fallout 3 Remaster Reportedly Still in 'Active Development,' New Starfield Content Out Soon Update 1:13pm PT: Iron Galaxy has taken to social media to deny the speculation that it's working on a Fallout: New Vegas remaster, or anything Fallout-related. Whoops.It turns out, the "Please Stand By" image is one that Iron Galaxy uses all the time in its company meetings, and is not indicative of any actual projects."Nope! There is nothing to see here," wrote the studio on Bluesky. "Sorry to disturb the volcanoes, but that was just a BTS look at our company meeting. We use that slide every month and has nothing to do with anything Fallout being worked on. As you can imagine, we love Fallout, too. Now pardon us as we retreat back into our vault."Original story continues below:Fallout fans are desperate for news on upcoming games in Bethesda's post-apocalyptic role-playing series, and it looks like a pretty solid tease has just dropped from a surprising source.Iron Galaxy Studios, perhaps most famous for working on Xbox fighting game Killer Instinct, issued a post on social media and LinkedIn that includes a pretty obvious tease that it’s working on something Fallout related.“Today’s our February company meeting. It’s time to catch up with what the company’s been up to and what’s coming up next for IG,” reads the post, alongside a picture of Fallout’s iconic “Please Stand By” holding image on a monitor, next to the same image in a slideshow presentation.Specifically, the image is of Fallout New Vegas' loading screen, which has sparked speculation that Iron Galaxy is working on the heavily rumored Fallout New Vegas remaster.Both Fallout 3 and New Vegas are reportedly set for the remaster treatment. The Fallout 3 remaster appeared in FTC documents as part of Microsoft’s bid to buy Activision Blizzard, although it remains unannounced. According to a report by The Verge, Bethesda is keen to ensure the game is polished enough to enjoy a successful launch similar to last year’s The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered, which Bethesda chief Todd Howard recently told IGN he was "really, really pleased" with.The Fallout: New Vegas remaster is also reportedly on the way, although apparently further down the line. Could Iron Galaxy be working on both games? It has form when it comes to supporting the development of Fallout. Iron Galaxy worked on both Fallout 4 VR and Fallout 76, so it knows the franchise. Meanwhile, it worked on other Bethesda games, including The Elder Scrolls Online, Skyrim on Switch, and Skyrim VR, so it knows Bethesda.Of course, this could be a tease for something else, but it does seem clear that Iron Galaxy is working on Fallout. Given the hyper interest in all things Fallout, it would be a tad misguided to post this image to social media and LinkedIn if you weren't working on Fallout!In a recent interview with IGN, we asked Bethesda development chief Todd Howard if the success of The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered, which has seen over 4 million players since it shadowdropped last year, was a repeatable trick for a Fallout 3 Remastered. Howard kept his cards close to his chest, and reiterated a point he’s been making a lot in interviews lately.“I will just say that the Oblivion Remaster, we're really, really pleased with how well it did, it was a very long project too, and not just in how it was received, the ability to shadowdrop it, and the response to doing that,” he said. “I like to do that with games as much as possible. I love the moment that you find out about a game.”The last mainline single-player Fallout game was Fallout 4, which came out in 2015 and recently saw the release of its Anniversary Edition. The multiplayer focused Fallout 76 followed in 2018, and while fans slowly flocked to the West Virginia-set open-world RPG, it wasn’t until the premiere of Prime Video’s Fallout TV show that the Bethesda series leveled up in terms of attention.As well as remasters, we know Bethesda wants to eventually get to Fallout 5, albeit after The Elder Scrolls 6. Back in June 2024, Todd Howard said he wasn’t interested in rushing Fallout 5 out the door. Then, in December last year, Howard confirmed that Fallout 5 would indeed take into account the canon events of the Fallout TV series. "In short, yes," Howard told BBC Newsbeat. "Fallout 5 will be existing in a world where the stories and events of the show happened or are happening. We are taking that into account."Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

title: Cyberpunk 2077 Headed to Xbox Game Pass, According to Microsoft Tease
body_text: Related reads:Cyberpunk 2077 VR Modder Hit by Another DMCA Strike, Pauses Patreon, Pulls Access to All His Mods, and Declares He's 'Under Attack' Microsoft has teased the arrival of Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Game Pass, via a social media post.While over five years old at this point, CD Projekt's sci-fi blockbuster would still be a notable addition to Microsoft's subscription service. As of yet, however, there's no word on when it might be added. In a post on social media last night, the official Xbox Game Pass account dropped numerous hints at a big addition to the service's catalog, while also dropping numerous mentions of "v" — which is, of course, the name of the game's main character. Something v cool is coming soon... pic.twitter.com/nO8xfHcufa— Xbox Game Pass (@XboxGamePass) March 2, 2026 "Something v cool is coming soon..." Microsoft teased. An attached image then shows a fictional internal email which describes "the latest upcoming addition" as "a v good one too" — with the "V" bolded.Reinforcing the tease, the email begins with "wake up social team," which is a reference to "Wake the f**k up, Samurai! We have a city to burn," the line delivered by Keanu Reeves as Johnny Silverhand in the 2019 Cyberpunk 2077 cinematic trailer.Cyberpunk 2077 has been available via PlayStation Plus since last summer, so its arrival onto Xbox Game Pass would not be a huge surprise. Perhaps the hope is that anyone who's not yet played the game will be given a sample of what CD Projekt has to offer, ahead of The Witcher 3's much-rumored new DLC that's expected to arrive later this year.Work is also underway on the game's full sequel, Cyberpunk 2, which does not yet have a release date, and The Witcher 4, which we know won't launch in 2026. After that, there's an ambitious roadmap to then launch The Witcher 5 and The Witcher 6 in relatively quick succession, wrapping up the series' second trilogy in just six years.For now, we'll keep an eye on Microsoft's Xbox Game Pass announcements and update again when Cyberpunk 2077 is made official.Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. title: Capcom Spotlight Presentation Set For Later This Week — Here's What Will Be Shown
body_text: Related reads:Mega Man: Dual Override The Game Awards 2025 Reveal Trailer - Screenshots Though millions of us are still busy with Resident Evil Requiem, it seems developer Capcom isn't content to leave us playing as Raccoon City's unluckiest cop for long — a presentation showing off what else the developer has in the works is set for Thursday, March 5.Capcom Spotlight is a digital event that brings us up to date on the latest news from Capcom and the developer's upcoming releases. Set for 2pm PT / 5pm ET / 10pm UK time), the half-hour show will be subtitled in 13 different languages. The 30-minute digital event will update us on several upcoming Capcom games, and in particular Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection, Pragmata, Street Fighter 6 Years 1-2 Fights Edition, Mega Man Starforce Legacy Collection, and Megaman Dual Override. Megaman Dual Override is, of course, the brand-new entry in the classic action platforming series expected to release next year, while Mega Man Star Force: Legacy Collection is a compilation of Mega Man video games, including Mega Man Star Force: Pegasus, Mega Man Star Force: Leo, Mega Man Star Force: Dragon, Mega Man Star Force: Zerker x Ninja, Mega Man Star Force: Zerker x Saurian, Mega Man Star Force 3: Black Ace, and Mega Man Star Force 3: Red Joker. (Phew!)Street Fighter 6: Years 1-2 Fighters Edition, currently expected in June, includes 26 characters released from Years 1 & 2, including their Outfit 1 Colors 3-10, and 20 stages (Alex is out later this month), while Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection tells the story of two nations on the path to ruin and the discovery of a mysterious egg gives cause for hope. It's out next month. Last but not least is Pragmata, an all-new sci-fi action adventure with its own unique hacking twist. Set in the near future, protagonists Hugh and his android companion Diana must work together as they make their way through the cold lunar research station.Of course, that's just what Capcom has confirmed will be shown — there's usually a surprise or two, too, so make sure to tune in on Thursday. On the subject of Capcom: we may now know the solution to Capcom's devious Resident Evil Requiem Final Puzzle, but a whole new mystery is just beginning for fans — one centered on Leon S. Kennedy, and a huge secret that's only hinted at in the game's closing moments. Here's what we know so far…Vikki Blake is a reporter for IGN, as well as a critic, columnist, and consultant with 15+ years experience working with some of the world's biggest gaming sites and publications. She's also a Guardian, Spartan, Silent Hillian, Legend, and perpetually High Chaos. Find her at BlueSky. Related reads:Mega Man: Dual Override - Official Reveal Trailer | The Game Awards 2025

title: Sådan planlægger du en filmaften med brætspil
body_text: Du er her: Annoncering | Sådan planlægger du en filmaften med brætspil Annoncørbetalt indhold 03. mar. 2026 | 22:30 Sådan planlægger du en filmaften med brætspil Foto | Bazoom AI At kombinere film med brætspil fra spilforsyningen.dk kan skabe en unik og engagerende oplevelse for både venner og familie. Ofte kan det være en udfordring at matche tempo og stemning eller undgå, at reglerne bliver for omfattende. Med grundig forberedelse kan du sikre, at både film og spil får optimale betingelser og bidrager til en vellykket aften. Det handler om at finde balancen mellem aktivitet og fordybelse, så hele aftenen forløber i et naturligt flow. Midt i præsentationen af mulighederne dukker sjove brætspil op som et element, der kan styrke det sociale samvær og trække alle ind i oplevelsen. Du bør overveje stemning og fortælleform, så film og brætspil understøtter hinanden og ikke trækker opmærksomheden væk fra det fælles projekt. At sammensætte en vellykket aften kræver derfor planlægning og sans for detaljen. Tre modeller Når du vil forene film med brætspil, kan du vælge forskellige strukturer for aftenen. Den klassiske model er at starte med at se film og efterfølgende samles om spillet, hvor filmens stemning kan præge valget af brætspil. Denne rækkefølge giver anledning til fælles refleksion og samtale, og der er mulighed for at snakke om filmoplevelsen, mens brætspillet gradvist samler gruppen igen. En anden tilgang er at begynde med brætspillet og afslutte med film. Så får energien og konkurrencen frit løb, hvorefter fællesskabet topper af med ro og fordybelse foran lærredet. En tredje mulighed er at inddele aftenen som en slags sandwich. Start med et kort brætspil til opvarmning, se en film, og afslut med endnu et lille og let brætspil. På den måde bruges spil som overgang og samlingspunkt før og efter filmens fortælling. Match mellem genre og spil Et velfungerende match mellem film og brætspil handler mindre om at vælge direkte licenser og mere om at fokusere på stemning og fortælleform. For eksempel kan science fiction-film bindes sammen med strategiske brætspil, hvor systemer, samarbejde og logik er centrale elementer. Noir-film passer ofte sammen med spil, der involverer hemmelige roller, deduktion og bluff, så dramaet og spændingen fortsætter fra lærred til spilleplade. Fantasy-film kan få følgeskab af spil, hvor rejser, eventyr og fælles progression er afgørende. Her gælder det om at vælge spil, der ikke kræver lange instruktioner, men hurtigt fanger opmærksomheden og holder gruppens interesse fra start til slut. Ved at matche genre og spiltype kan du skabe et flow, så oplevelsen føles hel og gennemført, uden at en af delene overskygger den anden. Praktiske rammer Gruppens størrelse, alder og erfaringsniveau bør styre valget af brætspil, så regler og spilletid passer til selskabets tålmodighed. Det hjælper også at vælge spil med få regler og begrænset forklaringstid, især hvis filmen fylder meget dramaturgisk. Bordplads, lys og snacks har stor betydning for oplevelsen og bør forberedes, så hele aftenen glider nemmere. Midt i planlægningen er det en fordel at afstemme pauser og overgange, så både film og spil får deres naturlige plads, og intet drukner i forklaringer. Lydniveau og atmosfære kan hurtigt sætte stemningen skævt, hvis for eksempel filmens intense lyd står i kontrast til samtaler under spillet. Skab derfor klare rammer, hvor alle ved, hvornår filmafsnittet starter, og hvornår der skal spilles. Med en enkel tjekliste, der omfatter struktur, genre-match, pauser og rammer, får både spillets flow og filmens dramaturgi de bedste betingelser for at forene sig i samme aften. title: Blå valgsejr vil betyde kraftigt reduceret DR
author: Af Øjvind Hesselager
body_text: Du er her: Artikler | Nyhed | Blå valgsejr vil betyde kraftigt reduceret DR RSS-feed / artikler Nyhed 03. mar. 2026 | 10:43 Blå valgsejr vil betyde kraftigt reduceret DR Foto | Marie Hald ”De dele af det nuværende DR, der kan klare sig på markedsvilkår, skal udskilles og lægges bag betalingsmur,” siger Liberal Alliances kulturordfører Katrine Daugaard og tilføjer, at det gælder størstedelen af DR’s indhold. Liberal Alliance vil skære godt to milliarder kroner i DR’s budget og privatisere kanalen. Tre andre borgerlige partier bakker op om en nedskæring. ”DR er en mastodont,” lyder det. Af Øjvind Hesselager Liberal Alliance mener, at DR har svigtet sin kerneopgave: at levere public service-indhold. Og når vi er forbi folketingsvalget, skal der skæres til benet. Altså hvis det står til partiet, der lige nu ser ud til at blive den største aktør i den borgerlige blok, og hvis formand Alex Vanopslagh i så tilfælde er kandidat til statsministerposten. Annonce ”De dele af det nuværende DR, der kan klare sig på markedsvilkår, skal udskilles og lægges bag betalingsmur. Og det er størstedelen af DR’s indhold. Det er indhold, der ikke skiller sig ud fra TV 2’s eller andre kanalers,” siger Liberal Alliances kulturordfører, 44-årige Katrine Daugaard, til Ekko. Står det til Liberal Alliance, skal de cirka 3,7 milliarder kroner, der i dag bruges på DR, reduceres til 1,5 milliarder kroner. En besparelse på 2.2 milliarder kroner. Og de resterende 1,5 milliarder kroner skal bruges på at udbyde reelt og snævert public service-indhold via tre tv-kanaler og de ti radiokanaler, vi i dag kender som P4. Liberal Alliance mener, at DR er gået i stå og løser opgaven helt forkert. ”DR er blevet for magelige, og fokus på kerneopgaven er gået fløjten,” siger Katrine Daugaard. Hun fremhæver DR’s nye plan, hvor der står, at ”DR vil prioritere musik, kultur og sport som samlingspunkter, der samler danskerne”. Hertil siger hun: ”Men DR skal ikke samle Danmark om Bagedysten og sportsbegivenheder. Det kan de gøre med Anders Agger eller de historiske dramadokumentarer, som de laver så flot. Det er jo i høj grad det kommercielle stof, der samler Danmark, ikke public service-programmerne. Hvis alt kaldes public service, mister ordet dets betydning.” ”Alle producenter kan jo lave indhold, der samler Danmark. Og TV 2 (finansieret af reklamer og abonnementer, red.) gør det allerede og er bedre til det end DR. TV 2 kan endda tjene penge på det. Hvorfor skal vi så bruge skatteborgernes penge på det? Det skal stoppe!” Fire milliarder kørt ind på paller Et gennemgående element i Liberal Alliances plan er, at DR skal drives efter et meget snævrere public service-begreb end i dag. ”Vi vil ind til benet af public service. Det er den helt snævre public service, der ikke kan klare sig på markedsvilkår. De programmer, vi giver hinanden i forhold til dannelse og kultur.” – Kan du være mere konkret? ”Det er for eksempel de store filmiske programmer om Grundtvig, programmer, der nærmest bliver undervisning. Dronninger og konger og vores fælles historie. Det er også grønlandske og færøske nyheder.” ”Grønlandske nyheder bliver sendt på den private kanal dk4 i dag. Det er jo en total falliterklæring for DR. dk4 bringer rigtigt meget stof, der er mere snævert public service end det meste af det, DR bringer. Dér kunne DR lære noget, selv om dk4 selvfølgelig ikke har DR’s kvalitet. Men det er selvfølgelig også nemmere at få det til at se professionelt ud, når man får knap fire milliarder kroner kørt ind på paller hvert år,” siger Katrine Daugaard. Hun mener i det hele taget, at DR har tabt vildskaben og kreativiteten på grund af de mange ledelseslag, som hun noterer, at den nye bestyrelse er i gang med at rydde op i. ”DR er en mastodont. Der er så mange ledere, at selv ansatte i DR ikke ved, hvem der bestemmer,” sammenfatter hun. Inden 100 dage Og det kan komme til at gå stærkt. Slankningen skal sættes i gang inden de første 100 dage efter regeringsoverdragelsen. Det fremgår af et fælles katalog fra Liberal Alliance, Konservative, Dansk Folkeparti og Danmarksdemokraterne under den samlede betegnelse ”Borgerligt Konvent”. ”Der skal laves en plan for et slankere DR, der fokuserer på kerneopgaverne,” lyder det således samstemmende fra de fire partier i udspillet. Katrine Daugaard understreger, at det ikke bare er en skarp markering på grund af valget. ”Vi har i den borgerlige opposition fundet 50 forslag, som vi er enige om at effektuere på de første 100 dage, skulle vi komme i regering. Et af dem er, at DR skal slankes,” siger hun. Næppe alle borgerlige partier vil skære lige så hårdt som Liberal Alliance, men alle er med på at sætte bevillingen til DR ned. ”Jeg tror ikke, at vores udspil bliver vedtaget, som det ligger. Men det gør heller ikke noget. Vi skal have sat gang i den debat og vise danskerne, at det kan gøres anderledes, og at vi tør være visionære.” siger Katrine Daugaard, der selv er uddannet musiker og har tæt kontakt til kulturlivet. Fantasiløs lighed I dag er alle danskere tvunget til at betale til DR via skatten. Det skal der sættes en stopper for, mener Liberal Alliance. ”Borgerne skal – modsat i dag – kunne fravælge DR, ligesom vi kender det på TV 2,” siger Katrine Daugaard. Indhold fra DR skal lægges bag betalingsmur, mener Liberal Alliance. ”Men de tre tv-kanaler, som så sendes i udbud, og som DR også vil kunne byde på, skal ligge frit tilgængeligt for alle danskere, ligesom DR’s bagkatalog også skal være det. Det har vi jo allerede betalt for.” Public service skal ifølge Liberal Alliance fremover leveres gennem private aktører, der byder ind på en eller flere af følgende områder: – nyheder, samfund og debat (primært fokus: live-tv og -radio) – kultur, historie og drama (primært fokus: tv og radio) – børn og unge (primært fokus: tv) – ti regionale stationer (primært fokus: live-radio) Liberal Alliance savner større forskellighed i DR’s nuværende regionale radiokanaler. ”I dag fremstår DR’s regionale kanaler næsten identiske på tværs af landet. Det er fantasiløst. Det kunne være spændende med vidt forskellige aktører,” siger kulturordføreren. Liberal Alliance mener, at et privatiseret DR skal kunne byde på de tre tv-stationer, som partiet mener, der skal være i public servicetilbuddet. ”De dygtige mennesker i DR, som vi har til at lave børne-tv, kan gå sammen og byde ind på den kanal. Det kunne også være, at nogle af de dygtige børnefilmproducenter, vi har i Danmark, kunne været interesseret. Men det er da bestemt også tænkeligt, at DR, som jo laver forrygende børne-tv, rent faktisk ville vinde dette udbud.” I det hele taget er det nicherne og dybden, DR skal dyrke i fremtiden, mener Liberal Alliance. ”DR skal lave graverjournalistik. Alt det dyre, som de private har svært ved at lave,” siger hun og understreger, at DR har forsømt at påtage sig oplagte public service-opgaver. ”Det er en kæmpe fadæse, at TV 2 News er skabt af TV 2 og ikke DR. DR har simpelthen sovet i timen.” Nedtælling til valget Ligesom det er uvist, om der bliver et borgerligt flertal efter valget, er det også usikkert, hvor stor besparelsen for DR bliver. ”Men hvis det står det til os, skal det være ganske meget,” siger Katrine Daugaard. ”I dag udkonkurrerer staten blandt andet de private dagblade. Det fremgår jo af DR’s egne fortrinlige medieanalyser. Dagbladene fylder uhyggeligt lidt i det samlede billede – også dem, der tjener penge. Og hvorfor købe abonnement på Politiken, når DR laver en flot og gratis onlineavis? DR skal ganske enkelt rammesættes meget hårdere. Ellers har vi ikke dagblade i nær fremtid,” siger Katrine Daugaard. ”Der er i den tid, vi lever i, ingen grund til, at have en dyr statsradiofoni. Vi kan jo i dag få gode, saglige nyheder fra mange dygtige og lødige danske medier.” Hun mener, hele den nuværende DR-konstruktion har politisk slagside. ”Når den nuværende SVM-regering, der er tilhænger af et stort statsligt DR, vil have en medieombudsmand, lugter det af, at politikerne vil have kontrol over medierne og stoppe journalister, der laver journalistik om politikerne. Men journalister skal jo kontrollere politikerne. Alt andet er jo den rene kommunisme.” – Det er hårde ord! ”Ja, men det er jo nærmest kommunistisk. Først at afsætte så mange milliarder kroner til et statsejet, venstredrejet medie og så bagefter ville styre indholdet på de andre medier ved at kunne begrænse dem gennem en medieombudsmand. Det er kommunistisk tankegods og ikke en fri nation værdigt.” Kommentarer danmarks radio, katrine daugaard, liberal alliance tilmeld nyhedsbrev Dit navn: Din email: Hvad er 1 + 2? title: Netflix-chef bryder tavsheden efter budkrig
author: Af Kevin Lundgreen Frederiksen
body_text: Du er her: Artikler | Nyhed | Netflix-chef bryder tavsheden efter budkrig RSS-feed / artikler Nyhed 03. mar. 2026 | 07:42 Netflix-chef bryder tavsheden efter budkrig Foto | Patrick T. Fallon Ted Sarandos peger på politisk pres under budkrigen om Warner Bros. Discovery og kalder Paramounts tilbud for irrationelle. ”Faktisk kan det måske ligefrem være en fordel for os. Men for branchens skyld håber jeg, at jeg tager fejl,” siger Ted Sarandos fra Netflix, der tabte budkrigen om Warner Bros. til Paramount. Af Kevin Lundgreen Frederiksen Da støvet lagde sig efter budkrigen om Warner Bros. Discovery, lignede det umiddelbart et prestigetab for Netflix. Streaminggiganten valgte ikke at matche Paramount Skydances forhøjede bud og måtte se drømmen om at føje HBO og Warner til sit katalog smuldre. Paramount hævede nemlig indsatsen markant og løftede Netflix’ oprindelige bud på omkring 82,7 milliarder dollars til omkring 111 milliarder – svarende til 31 dollars per aktie. Annonce Men aktiemarkedet så noget helt andet. Det viser sig nemlig, at Netflix-aktien steg over ti procent, og selskabets markedsværdi voksede med omkring 35 milliarder dollars – lige under halvdelen af, hvad Paramount nu skal betale for Warner. I et interview med mediet Bloomberg lægger Netflix-direktør Ted Sarandos ikke skjul på, hvad han mener om budprocessen og prisen, Paramount endte med at betale. ”Usædvanligt, ja, usædvanligt, irrationelt – hvilke ord man nu vil bruge om det,” siger han ifølge branchebladet Variety og fortsætter: ”Det bliver fascinerende at se, hvad det næste skridt bliver. Jeg har gentagne gange de seneste to uger udtalt mig om, hvordan jeg mener, fremtiden kommer til at se ud. Jeg er overbevist om, at vi står stærkt, og at vi ikke bliver påvirket af alt det her. Faktisk kan det måske ligefrem være en fordel for os. Men for branchens skyld håber jeg, at jeg tager fejl.” Pres fra TrumpTed Sarandos forholder sig også til, at den amerikanske præsident Donald Trumps undervejs har lagt pres på handlen. ”Det er langt billigere at lave larm end rent faktisk at hæve sit bud. Så de prøvede den strategi først. Da det så gik op for dem, at vi ikke var i CNN-foretagendet, blev det langt mindre interessant,” fortæller han. Donald Trump har tidligere langet ud efter CNN for deres dækning af hans embedsværk. I december gav han udtryk for, at mediet burde sælges som en del af enhver aftale med Warner Bros. I samme ombæring fik han også kaldt de drivende kræfter bag CNN ”korrupte og inkompetente”. Samtidig har han også offentlig angrebet Netflix og truet selskabet politisk. Ifølge Ted Sarandos valgte Netflix netop at trække stikket, fordi selskabet havde fastlagt en meget klar ramme for, hvad man var villig til at betale. ”Vi havde et meget snævert interval for, hvad vi var villige til at betale, og vi afgav allerede det tilbud, da vi indgik i aftalen.” ”Vi havde ikke rykket os meget fra det, bortset fra at vi gik over til kontant betaling, hvilket var med til at få handlen hurtigere i hus. Jeg er tilfreds med den pris, vi gik ind til, og tilfreds med den pris, vi gik ud med. Vi vidste med det samme, da vi torsdag fik besked om, at der lå et bedre tilbud, og fik detaljerne om den aftale. Vi vidste præcis, hvad vi ville gøre.” I forbindelse med buddet på Warner Bros. har Netflix ændret sin oprindelige kontant- og aktiebaserede betaling til et ”all-cash”-bud, hvor aktionærerne udelukkende får udbetalt kontanter for deres aktier. Det betyder, at de ikke modtager aktier i Netflix, men i stedet får et fast beløb med det samme. Det er typisk mere attraktivt, fordi det sikrer værdi uden risiko for udsving i aktiekurserne. Skabere frem for købereDerudover får Netflix et økonomisk plaster på såret. Aftalen med Warner Bros. indeholdt nemlig et break up-fee. I praksis betyder det, at Warner Bros. Discovery – og senere Paramount, som overtog processen – skal betale Netflix omkring 2,8 milliarder dollars, da streaminggiganten trak sig fra handlen. Beløbet fungerer som kompensation for den tid og de ressourcer, Netflix nåede at investere i forhandlingerne. Og ifølge Ted Serandos er det usandsynligt, at Netflix vil kaste sig ud i en lignende sammenslutning i fremtiden. Og den store pose penge fra Paramount skal bruges på at ”investere i virksomheden”. ”Vi er skabere, ikke købere. Alt det er stadig sandt,” lyder det fra topdirektøren.
